text:
Nora (People Ops): quick thread re: backup childcare pool + emergency shift swaps during parental leave. manager asked whether we reimburse backup care and how to handle short-notice shift coverage. TL;DR: yes we have a backup-care vendor list + limited reimbursement, and managers approve shift swaps.
Emma: thanks! curious about the reimbursement cap and the documentation we need?
Nora (People Ops): we reimburse up to $300/month for licensed backup care when it's used for approved parental-leave-related coverage (e.g., unexpected daycare closure, medical appointment for child). need receipt and provider confirmation (date/time, caregiver name).
Devon: is the $300/month per family or per child?
Nora (People Ops): per family. exceptions possible for extraordinary circumstances with manager + People Ops approval.
Ivy (Manager): for shift swaps, can an IC trade shifts with another team member while on phased return? any payroll/OT implications?
Nora (People Ops): yes, informal shift swaps allowed if both managers sign off and the swap is documented via the Shift Swap Form. Payroll will treat swapped hours as normal pay for the person who worked them; overtime rules still apply.
Finance Bot: Note: backup-care reimbursements are treated as taxable income in the U.S. unless paid directly to an IRS-qualified provider via our vendor platform. If reimbursed to the employee, payroll will include it in the next paycheck with appropriate taxes.
Devon: so better to use the vendor platform when possible?
Nora (People Ops): correct. we maintain an approved vendor list (on the intranet) that can invoice Redwood directly which avoids taxing the employee in many regions. link: https://intranet.redwood/family/backup-care (vendor list + booking flow).
Global HR - EMEA: heads-up for EMEA folks: local country rules differ. In some countries we can pay providers directly or offer non-taxable vouchers; check the local HR rep before paying anything.
Emma: how do managers request the reimbursement exception if someone goes over $300 in a month?
Nora (People Ops): submit an exception request: include employee name, dates, reason, receipts, and manager justification. People Ops + Finance review within 5 business days. minimal fields below to paste into an email:
```
Backup Care Exception Request
Employee: <name>
Month: <YYYY-MM>
Total amount requested: $XXX.XX
Reason: <e.g., extended closure due to weather>
Manager approver: <name>
Attachments: receipts, provider confirmation
```
Nora (People Ops): also note: for emergency shift coverage while on leave, managers should consider temporary agency or contractor coverage if swaps would cause burnout. Hiring panel and SOW templates are on the hiring portal.
Ivy (Manager): final quick one: do we require staff to use their PTO for backup care during parental leave?
Nora (People Ops): no. when the backup care is directly linked to parental leave or phased return, we do not force PTO. But if an employee misses work unrelated to parental responsibilities, PTO rules apply. People Ops can advise on edge cases.
Devon: thanks all — i'll book through the vendor platform next time and save receipts.
Nora (People Ops): great. i'll update the leave packet with the vendor flow, reimbursement cap, exception process, and shift-swap checklist. ping me if you want me to pre-approve before booking. :white_check_mark:
